title: OpenHydroLab: interactive, physics-accurate animations for teaching fluid mechanics, hydraulics and hydrology

creators.name: Das, Samiran
creators.affiliation: James Watt School of Engineering, University of Glasgow (Singapore campus)

description:
OpenHydroLab is an open-source suite of ten interactive browser laboratories for teaching undergraduate fluid mechanics, hydraulics and hydrology. Every displayed quantity is computed live from the governing equation, and every module runs offline from a local file, with no installation and no third-party host. Eight modules are single self-contained HTML pages; the two 3D laboratories are a page plus a vendored copy of Three.js under animations/vendor/three/, which must be kept alongside them.

Modules. Fluid statics: hydrostatic forces on plane and curved surfaces, and hydrostatic force in three dimensions. Open-channel hydraulics: channel geometry and the Froude number, specific energy and choking, hydraulic jumps, Manning uniform flow, gradually varied flow profiles. Hydrology: storm hydrographs, the unit hydrograph workbench, and an IDF/frequency-analysis pipeline on a real 27-year gauge record.

Release 1.0.3 opens the fluid mechanics section with the two hydrostatic-forces laboratories, and extends the verification harness from the numbers a module reports to the geometry it draws: arrows retain the line segment they were constructed from, and cases assert against those recorded endpoints rather than against a recomputation of what they ought to be. The harness now records 194 distinct numerical cases, executed across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit to yield 582 comparison records, together with 108 software, offline-delivery and accessibility checks repeated on the three engines (324 runs), with none failing. Every reference value is derived independently of the code. The protocol is documented in validation/validation-protocol.md and the generated dataset in validation/results/.

This protocol establishes computational fidelity and reproducibility only; it makes no claim about learning outcomes.
